title: This Great Lakes Cryptid Has Been Hiding for Over 200 Years
excerpt: Turns out Michigan doesn't have to look all the way to Scotland for a lake monster of its own.
content:
When people talk about cryptids or monsters, a few have worldwide acclaim: Bigfoot, Mothman, and the Loch Ness Monster are perhaps the most popular. As a kid who grew up watching Scooby-Doo on the daily, my all-time favorite movie was Scooby-Doo and the Loch Ness Monster. Nessie holds a special place in my heart, even though she lives way over in Scotland.

So imagine my shock when I learned there might be a Loch Ness Monster living in Lake Erie. Not just an old campfire story, but a monster that saw a huge wave of activity as recently as 1990, so credible that it sent hundreds flocking to the lakeshore in hopes of photographing the monster for the first time.

Bessie, The Lake Erie Monster

Despite Lake Erie being the shallowest of the Great Lakes, apparently a huge monster has managed to stay hidden this whole time. Spotted for the first time in 1793, Bessie is said to be a 30-foot serpent that "hisses" and "has a tremendous tail," according to an alleged sighting published in a newspaper in 1818.

But the most intriguing part of this local legend is a recent craze in 1990. A Los Angeles Times article from 1990 highlights the story of Harold Bricker, who claimed to see a large black creature moving in the water, measuring 35 feet long.

Bricker's report led to a flurry of other reports, prompting local Thomas Solberg to offer a $5000 reward to anyone who captured Bessie alive. The reward brought people from all around to try and find her, but ultimately amounted to nothing.

Still, it's quite wild that a mythical creature could stir up such a ruckus in our modern time. The Appalachian Historian recently did a massive deep dive on the Lake Erie Monster; if you'd like to learn more, you should check out their article.
